title: Ephemeral key bleed diagnosis and graceful OOM slowdown for Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted and dedicated pools, plus one private deployment) reported sudden GPU OOM waves accompanied by steady growth of ephemeral key allocations in the runtime key-index. Symptoms pointed at a KV index state where short-lived session keys were never reclaimed ("key bleed"), causing fragmentation and preventing the evictor from freeing contiguous GPU arenas, ultimately triggering OOMs under normal load.

Environments affected: hosted-api (us-west1), dedicated-gpu-pools (eu-west), private-vpc-customer-7.

Observed behavior: after a burst of chat/generation traffic with many short-lived sessions (typical PLG warmup), metrics showed unbounded rise in kv_ephemeral_allocs, tombstone_ratio stayed low, and slab_free_contiguous dropped until allocator returned OOM for large tensor requests. Heap profiles and GPU memory maps show many small allocations tied to session prefixes still referenced by stale index entries. Core dumps for one dedicated node show free list scatter and increased malloc churn.

Reproducer notes: internal reproducer using workload generator (workloads/short_session_spike) reproduces the drift in ~15-20 minutes with 1000 concurrent short sessions. Reproducer script and dataset: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reproducers/tree/main/short_session_spike

Root cause hypothesis: race between prefix eviction and async journal flush that can leave ephemeral key entries in a "limbo" state: visible to runtime (preventing reclaim) but not reachable by normal lookups for eviction. This prevents tombstone compaction from folding those entries and prevents the allocator from coalescing adjacent slabs, causing fragmentation and eventual OOM when large contiguous tensors are requested.

Immediate mitigations applied (triage window):
- Enabled emergency evictor backpressure on affected pools (reduced new session admission rate by 30%).
- Deployed a CLI hotpatch to aggressively mark stale prefix tombstones as reclaimable after 60s of inactivity (hosted canary at 5% traffic).
- For Dedicated customers we increased per-tenant session-ttl and lowered session retention default to allow earlier eviction; for Private customer we provided a config to trigger immediate tombstone sweep.

Longer-term fix proposed: runtime patch that introduces a two-phase reclaim protocol: (1) an index-level sanity-check that scans recently-flushed journal ranges and reconciles orphaned ephemeral keys, converting limbo entries to tombstones, and (2) an allocator coalescer repair that proactively merges adjacent free slabs during low-pressure windows. The fix includes a small state-machine modification to ensure the journal flush reports are atomic with prefix removal.

Design trade-offs: full synchronous journal+evict would be safest but adds latency; chosen approach favors eventual consistency with a short opportunistic reconciliation to avoid latencies in the common-case. We will gate the reconciliation and coalescer repair behind a runtime feature-flag for gradual rollout.

Rollout plan:
- PR and unit tests (runtime-1.19 branch) -> internal review (ETA 2 days).
- Canary (5%) on hosted-us-west1 for 48h with heavy short-session traffic and telemetry flags enabled.
- Expand to Dedicated non-production pools and one Private staging node after green canary.
- 2-step fullscreen rollout with rollback hooks: if kv_tombstone_rate decreases and allocator fragmentation metric improves by 30%, continue to 50% then 100%.

Monitoring & dashboards to add: kv_ephemeral_allocs, kv_limbolist_count, tombstone_compaction_rate, slab_coalescer_ops, contiguous_free_bytes, gpu_oom_events_by_node, evictor_backpressure_pct. Alert thresholds defined in runtime-ops playbook.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/infra/pages/34567/Ephemeral+Key+Bleed+Diagnosis+and+Reconciliation
- Reproducer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reproducers/tree/main/short_session_spike
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
- Incident timeline & postmortem stub: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDefG2/example

Next steps: land PR with unit + integration tests, run canary, monitor for regression, follow up with a postmortem and add preventive tests in CI to simulate short-session bursts and ensure tombstone reconciliation triggers.
